Author: Juvvadi Sridevi
Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi
 Criminal Revision Case No.956 Of 2008
Order:

This Criminal Revision Case, under Sections 397 and 401 of Cr.P.C., is filed by the petitioner/appellant, challenging the judgment, dated 01.07.2008, passed in Criminal Appeal No.25 of 2007 by the learned I Additional Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar, whereby, the conviction and sentence of rigorous imprisonment for a period of Six months and also sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine, to suffer simple imprisonment for one month for the offence punishable under Section 2(ia) (m) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w 16 (1)
(a) of PFA Act, 1954 imposed against the petitioner/appellant/accused No.1 by the learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet, vide judgment, dated 18.01.2007, passed in C.C.No.310 of 2002 was confirmed.
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The case of the prosecution, in brief, is as follows:
The petitioner/accused No.1 is running a Tea Depot at Narayanapet.

On 28.12.2001,
PW1/Complainant-Food Inspector inspected the said Tea Depot along with PW3- K.Vijaya Kumar and purchased 450 grams of tea powder for Rs.26-10 ps., and obtained cash receipt from accused No.1, sealed the said tea powder under cover of panchanama by following due procedure and on further enquiry, the complainant came to know that the said tea powder was supplied by A2 and A3.
After seizure of the samples, he sent the same for analysis and public analyst after examination,
found that it contained iron filings and as such it is adulterated.

Subsequently, the complainant obtained written consent for initiating prosecution against the accused person and thereafter, complaint was filed by PW1-Food Inspector against the petitioner herein along with A2 and A3.
3.
The accused were examined under Section 251 Cr.P.C., and substance of accusation was stated to them.
Accused pleaded not guilty of the offence alleged and claimed to be tried.
During the course of trial, prosecution examined P.Ws.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.32.
On behalf of the petitioners/accused, no evidence, either oral or documentary, has been adduced.

entities.text: M.A. Mubeen, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., Trgh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After a thoughtful consideration of the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the trial Court found the petitioner/accused No.1 guilty and convicted under Section 255 (2) Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under Section 2(ia) (m) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w 16 (1) (a)
of PFA Act, 1954 and accordingly sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of Six months and also sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one month.

However, the trial Court found Accused A-2 and A-3 not guilty and acquitted under Section 255 (1) Cr.P.C., for the offence under Section 2 (ia) (m)
punishable under Section 16 (1) (a) (i) of PFA Act, 1954, by judgment dated 18.01.2007.
Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner herein preferred Criminal Appeal No.25 of 2007 on the file of I Additional Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar.

However, the learned I-Additional Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar,
after re-appreciating the entire material available on record, dismissed the appeal, by confirming the conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
Hence the present Criminal Revision Case.

5. Heard Sri Bajrang Singh Thakur, the learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.1 and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent - State and perused the record.
6.

The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that this Criminal Revision Case is filed challenging the conviction of the petitioner/accused No.1, under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of PFA Act, 1954 on the allegations for selling the Tea Powder containing iron filings on 12.09.2006 to the Food Inspector.

Pending the disposal of the present criminal revision case, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, New Delhi, in File No.12 (4)2016/Misc./Enf/FSSAI, dated 02.11.2017, on thorough examination by FSSAI, felt that till a reliable method of assessment/testing of Iron filings in tea is finalized, it would not be appropriate to launch prosecution for non-conformance nor is it proper to pursue or continue with the prosecutions launched under PFA Ac/FSS Act prior to issue of FSSAI's Order dated 19.05.2016.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The Commissioners of Food Safety, All States/UTs are, therefore,
directed not to launch prosecutions for non- conformance of limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016.
They are also advised to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954.

As per the said orders, the present criminal revision case, is deserved to be allowed in view of the aforementioned order and requested the Hon'ble Court to allow the present criminal revision case and set aside the conviction of the petitioner for the offence in C.C.No.310 of 2002 dated 15.01.2007 of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet, in the interest of justice.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. The learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent - State submitted that as per the orders dated 02.11.2017 issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the Commissioners of Food Safety of all the States were directed not to launch for non-conformance of limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016 and were advised to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In view of the above, he submits that the prosecution of the petitioner in the present case would not survive and prays for passing appropriate orders.

8. Keeping in view of the orders dated 02.11.2017 the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submits that as he was instructed by the Food Safety Officer, Mahabubnagar to withdraw all the cases launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under the FSS Act or PFA Act and prosecution of the M.A. Mubeen, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., Trgh ... on 26 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110049848/
2 petitioner does not survive and is not maintainable.
9.

entities.text: M.A. Mubeen, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., Trgh

sentences.text: Having regard to the above said facts and circumstances, the Criminal Revision Case is allowed by setting aside the Judgment of the learned I Additional Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar, dated 01.07.2008 in Crl.A.No.25 of 2007 as well as conviction and sentence imposed against the petitioner/appellant/accused No.1 by the learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet vide its Judgment dated 18.01.2007 in C.C.No.310 of 2002.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this Criminal Revision Case, shall stand closed.

JUVVADI SRIDEVI, J.
